messages:
alex: heads up — noticed steady mem growth in KV cache on long-context runs (>> 16k tokens). not regular leak, looks like fragmentation + paging spikes when GC/evict kicks in
riley: can you paste the small repro or perf output? which allocator path is used in these runs?
alex: repro is simple: run the streaming chat sim for ~8h with many long histories. attach a small sample log: 
```
ALLOC_STATS: microchunk_allocs=2.3M microchunk_free=1.9M avg_chunk_bytes=372 frag_ratio=0.27 page_faults=1184
KV_CACHE: live_slots=430k used_bytes=3.2GB reserved_overhead=640MB
```
noting lots of small frees and new allocs, and `avg_chunk_bytes` sitting near 372 which is awkward for our buddy rounding
sam: hmm 372 bytes avg is weird — looks like our small-block path (<=512) is scattering into 64/128/256 bins depending on request shape. maybe we ended up with many 256+116 allocations => internal slack
alex: yes and the allocator coalescer seems hesitant since adjacent chunks have difftag lifetimes. result: many tiny holes that don't get reused -> paging when headroom low
riley: did anything change recently that would increase small live-churn?
perf-bot: regression detected: commit 7c4b3f3 (kernel selection heuristics) increased average request latency by 4% for long contexts; memory churn up 12% in KV tests
sam: that kernel commit changed batching windows and ended up increasing per-request kv-cache key lifetimes slightly (longer KV retention), so more overlap across sequences -> more fragmentation possible
alex: concrete idea: introduce microchunk genealogy metric and a tiny compact pass that coalesces adjacent free microchunks when fragmentation ratio > 0.15 and free run > 128KB. cheap check on alloc/free path (lock-free probe)
riley: agree on metric. also consider tuning block-size bucketing: move threshold boundaries so avg_chunk 372 maps to stable 384 rather than 256+slack. reduces cross-bin neighbors
sam: proposal: patch allocator: round-up to 32B granularity for <=1KB, stop strict buddy pairing for small runs, and add opportunistic in-place sweep on eviction (only when server idle <5% CPU). avoids large compaction pauses
alex: i'll prototype micro-compact in the runtime and a prometheus metric `kv_microchunk_frag_rate` + `kv_free_run_bytes_hist`
perf-bot: suggested canary: roll to a single dedicated pool with synthetic long-context workload, watch page faults and p95 latencies for 24h
devops-bot: deploying canary pool now (token: canary-evict-4). notify @sam @alex when finished
riley: also want an experiment toggling quantized kernel path: if kernel selection caused longer kv lifetimes, toggle it and compare frag metrics
alex: plan of action: 1) add metrics + cheap compact pass (PR today) 2) canary roll (tomorrow) 3) if frag drops -> ship allocator tuning; if not -> deeper trace + heaplet snapshots
sam: noted. i'll own allocator PR. alex + riley: owning canary and metrics. thanks :thumbsup:
alex: cheers — will post PR link and a short runbook for ops.
